text:
elaine-sales: FYI Lyra Health sent the full RFP earlier — they want a 2-week eval and are demanding on-prem option + customer-managed keys/HSM. I uploaded the packet: https://drive.redwood/lyra/rfp_2026.zip. Who can own the capability matrix + POC playbook?

mike-se: I can take the matrix. Quick clarifying Qs: do they explicitly require FedRAMP or just SOC2/BAA? Also any hard data residency (US-only?) constraints?

tori-sol-eng: Cover email mentions SOC2 + HIPAA and "FedRAMP-equivalent controls". They flagged several controls in the security questionnaire about HSM-backed keys and separation of duties. Data residency = US East only per their legal note.

sam-security: We support CMK via cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) but that requires an ops window. Need to confirm Lyra's HSM model/version and whether they expect in-week HSM provisioning. I'll draft section answers for encryption, key rotation, access logs, and attestations.

nina-legal: We can provide SOC2 Type II report and a BAA. We don't have FedRAMP accreditation; suggest we map our controls to their FedRAMP checklist and provide a gap table + mitigation. If they insist on FedRAMP, that's an escalation to enterprise.

aj-eng: For the POC itself, recommended baseline config to meet latency/throughput expectations: Dedicated pool of 2xA100 (or equivalent), model quantized to int8, 4k token cap. If they want on-prem Private with HSM, recommend 3-4 week lead time for procurement and network peering. Quick cost ballpark for 2-week POC (Dedicated): ~$24k total (includes reserved burst + ingress egress and engineer support).

jordan-sales-eng: We should be explicit about what we can deliver in the first 2 weeks vs what will come later. Suggest: Week 0-1 = Hosted/Dedicated POC w/ cloud KMS (CMK), Week 2-4 = Private + HSM migration plan. Lyra likely wants to validate data residency and key control first — cloud CMK in AWS (us-east-1) probably acceptable initial demo.

elaine-sales: Action items then: mike — matrix by EOD tomorrow; tori+sam — security questionnaire drafts (encrypt at rest, KMS/HSM, logging, retention); nina — BAA + SOC2 export; aj — full POC cost breakdown + runbook; jordan — prepare customer outreach message + timeline. I'll own outreach and executive summary.

elaine-sales: Attached files for reference: rfp_lyra_v1.xlsx, lyra_poc_playbook_v3.pdf (links in drive).

deploy-bot: file uploaded: rfp_lyra_v1.xlsx (drive://sales/lyra/rfp_lyra_v1.xlsx)

mike-se: Quick note for the capability matrix — I'll include columns: feature, supported (yes/no), notes (workarounds), SLA, compliance evidence (doc links), deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

tori-sol-eng: Security snippet to include in questionnaire answer: ```
EncryptionAtRest: AES-256-GCM
KMS: supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault; BYOK via PKCS#11 for on-prem HSMs
KeyRotation: customer-controlled (recommended 90 days)
AuditLogs: token-level audit + request traces (90 day retention by default)
```

sam-security: Addendum: for Private we can support HSMs that expose PKCS#11 or KMIP. We'll need network ports and an ops window. I'll list supported vendors and a short nexus guide.

nina-legal: I'll extract the specific questionnaire sections we can't answer from the sheet and flag them (exporting to a 1page exceptions doc). If they need FedRAMP attestation, we should push for an exceptions + roadmap instead of immediate compliance claim.

aj-eng: Cost/runbook draft will include: provisioning steps, test prompts, benchmarking script, perf targets, rollback steps. Sample command for on-prem KMS test: ```
redwood local-kms test --type pkcs11 --module /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so --pin 1234
```

jordan-sales-eng: I'll draft the customer-facing schedule and send it after we have the matrix. Proposed customer message: short, outlines week-by-week deliverables and clearly sets expectations on HSM timeline.

elaine-sales: One more blocker to call out — Lyra asked for model eval docs (accuracy/regression history) and a comparitive capability table vs their incumbent vendor. Mike, include a small eval summary and attach any relevant eval reports.

mike-se: Will do. I have an internal eval report (2025-q4) that'll fit. I'll redact PII and attach.

tori-sol-eng: For the onboarding checklist, we should include network peering IP ranges, required open ports, and sample Terraform snippet for peering. Small example: ```
resource "redwood_vpc_peering" "lyra" {
  vpc_id = "vpc-lyra-123"
  region = "us-east-1"
}
```

elaine-sales: Great. Plan: internal send tomorrow 9am PT with matrix + security/POC timeline. If no blockers, I'll share to Lyra around 11am PT.

jordan-sales-eng: noted — I'll be on the call if they want an immediate sync.

sam-security: I'll also prepare a short control mapping table to FedRAMP-equivalent items to preempt the ask.

elaine-sales: Thanks all. Short thread—please drop updates in this thread and attach your docs so I can stitch them into the RFP response pack. :thumbsup:
